strengths: Compelling and intuitive concept: replacing the heuristic, iterative splitting/cloning densification process of 3DGS with a geometrically informed, dense correspondence-based initialization from multi-view stereo pairs.

Strong empirical performance: achieves notable improvements in perceptual quality (e.g., LPIPS drops from 0.215 in 3DGS to 0.141 on Mip-NeRF 360) and competitive PSNR/SSIM across multiple benchmarks (Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending) with comparable or fewer Gaussians.

Fast convergence: demonstrated rapid convergence in early iterations (5k/10k steps) that outperforms or matches specialized accelerated frameworks, with initialization overhead explicitly tracked and included in reported timings (~120s on A100).

Insightful analysis and ablations: the paper offers thoughtful investigations into parameter trajectories (showing Gaussian coordinate drift is reduced up to 50x), robustness to coordinate/color perturbations, different feature matchers (RoMa, LoFTR, DKM), and depth-based alternatives.
Compatibility: convincingly demonstrates that EDGS initialization acts as a plug-and-play enhancement for existing adaptive density control methods (AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, Taming-3DGS).
weaknesses: Pruning mechanics and retention: While the paper eliminates splat cloning and splitting (densification), opacity-based pruning is still active. The role and dynamics of pruning during training are not analyzed in as much detail as initialization.

Triangulation and baseline considerations: The selection of 2 nearest neighbors based on camera pose proximity does not explicitly account for triangulation angle / baseline geometry. When baseline is very small (leading to high depth uncertainty) or wide (leading to occlusions/matching failure), triangulation can degrade.

Notational and matrix formulation discrepancies in Section 3.3: Projection matrices $P^i$ are defined as $\mathbb{R}^{4 \times 3}$ in the text but listed as $\mathbb{R}^{3 \times 4}$ in Table A9; the row/column conventions in Eq. (4)-(7) for setting up $A g_k^x = -b$ are somewhat inconsistent (e.g., mixing row vector projections with homogeneous solve).

strengths: The core idea of bypassing iterative heuristic densification via dense correspondence-based triangulation and sampling is conceptually clean, well-motivated, and challenges standard practice in 3DGS.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: the proposed method demonstrates strong rendering fidelity (notably in LPIPS and fine structural details) across Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending, both in densification-free mode and when serving as an initialization for other adaptive density control (ADC) frameworks.
Fast convergence: EDGS reaches high perceptual and photometric quality within 5k–10k steps, matching or exceeding several dedicated acceleration techniques.

In-depth analysis and insightful diagnostics: the paper provides thorough ablations on matcher choices, component contributions (confidence vs. geometric error), parameter trajectory lengths / displacement statistics (Fig. 4), and robustness under synthetic noise perturbations.
weaknesses: Dependence on pre-trained neural matchers: Unlike standard 3DGS which directly consumes the sparse SfM point cloud produced during pose estimation, EDGS introduces an extra dependency on heavy pre-trained matching networks (e.g., RoMa), adding peak GPU memory overhead (~15 GB) and an extra preprocessing pipeline.

Overall wall-clock training savings at convergence are modest: At the full 30k iterations (Table 1), EDGS takes 27 minutes on Mip-NeRF 360 compared to 26 minutes for standard 3DGS*, meaning the primary speedup benefit is strictly realized under early-stopping regimes (5k/10k steps).

Scalability to large-scale/unbounded environments: While restricting neighbor evaluation to 2 nearest neighbors keeps the matching cost bounded, pairwise dense feature extraction and pseudo-inverse SH solving across all reference views may become cumbersome for massive aerial or city-scale captures with thousands of views.

Minor mathematical notation inconsistency: In Section 3.3, camera projection matrices are defined as $P^i \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 3}$ using row-vector multiplication $[g_k^x, 1] P^i$, whereas Table A9 defines $P^i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 4}$, which is slightly confusing given conventional computer vision conventions.

strengths: Addresses an important and fundamental bottleneck in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the reliance on heuristic, iterative densification schemes that lead to long optimization trajectories and suboptimal convergence in high-frequency regions.

The dense initialization scheme is well-formulated, combining geometric reprojection filtering, confidence-based uniform sampling across views, and direct spherical harmonics (SH) regression from multi-view observations.

Strong empirical results across standard benchmarks (Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending): EDGS outperforms standard 3DGS and competitive baselines with significantly improved perceptual quality (LPIPS) and faster convergence (competitive at 5k–10k steps), all without densification.

Demonstrates versatile integration as a plug-and-play initialization for existing adaptive density control methods (e.g., AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, Taming 3DGS), consistently improving their performance without runtime penalties.

Comprehensive experimental analysis and ablations, including Gaussian parameter trajectory analysis (Fig. 4), matching algorithm comparisons (Tab. 5), robustness to synthetic coordinate/color noise (Fig. 7), and comparisons against alternative initialization schemes such as monocular depth (Tab. 7).
weaknesses: Reliance on external heavy 2D matching priors: The method shifts computational and architectural dependencies to a pre-trained dense matching network (RoMa), requiring ~15 GB GPU memory and forward inference across multiple view pairs. Although the overhead is accounted for in total training time (~120s), the system's performance is inherently bounded by the generalization and failure modes of the 2D matcher.

Handling of low-texture / non-Lambertian regions: The manuscript does not sufficiently analyze failure cases where dense stereo matchers struggle, such as large untextured surfaces (e.g., blank walls, skies) or specular/transparent surfaces where correspondence confidence is low or reprojection error is ill-defined.

Disproportionate improvement across metrics: While LPIPS shows substantial improvement (e.g., 0.141 vs. 0.215 on Mip-NeRF 360), PSNR improvements are much more modest (28.02 vs. 27.49 dB). The paper would benefit from a more detailed analysis explaining whether this gap stems from high-frequency texture hallucination/placement vs. exact geometric alignment.

Minor notation inconsistencies: In Sec. 3.3, projection matrices are defined as $P \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 3}$ to act on row vectors $[g_k^x, 1]$, whereas Table A9 lists $P^i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 4}$, which can create minor confusion regarding conventional projection dimensions.

strengths: The core idea—bypassing the slow, heuristic-driven iterative densification of 3DGS by densely initializing Gaussians via triangulated dense 2D correspondences—is intuitive, well-motivated, and practically impactful.

Comprehensive experimental validation on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending shows that EDGS reaches competitive or better rendering quality (especially SSIM and LPIPS) with up to 40% fewer Gaussians and significantly faster convergence.
The approach demonstrates orthogonality and composability, easily integrating with existing acceleration backends such as Taming-3DGS to yield further speedups.

Insightful analysis and ablations, including tracking parameter travel distance in coordinate/color space (Fig. 5), evaluating different dense matching models (Tab. 3), noise injection robustness (Fig. 6), and hyperparameter sweeps.
weaknesses: Mathematical formulation error in Section 3.3: In Equations (5)–(7), the linear triangulation system is formulated as $A g_k^x = -b$ for $g_k^x \in \mathbb{R}^3$, but Equation (6) sets $b = [0, 0, 0, 0]^T$. Solving $\arg\min \|A g_k^x + 0\|^2$ yields the trivial solution $g_k^x = 0$. For inhomogeneous DLT triangulation, the constants coming from the 4th column of the projection matrices must form a non-zero vector $b$.

Lack of clarity on Gaussian pruning: The manuscript emphasizes that densification is disabled, yet Figure A5 shows the Gaussian count declining steadily during optimization. The authors should explicitly clarify whether opacity-based pruning or opacity reset is retained, as 'densification' and 'pruning' are separate parts of 3DGS adaptive density control.

Scalability and dependency on pair selection: Dense pairwise matching using large neural networks (such as RoMa) incurs a non-negligible cost that scales with the number of view pairs. While the authors include this overhead in the total time for the tested benchmarks, the scalability to very large scenes with thousands of images without full multi-view consistency filtering remains unclear.

strengths: A conceptually simple and compelling idea: replacing the heuristic, iterative densification process (cloning/splitting) in 3DGS with a one-shot dense point initialization derived from modern dense 2D feature matching (RoMa).

Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments across multiple standard benchmarks (Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending), showing competitive or superior reconstruction quality (particularly on SSIM and LPIPS) with up to 40% fewer Gaussians.

Demonstrated compatibility and orthogonality with other 3DGS acceleration frameworks (e.g., Taming 3DGS, gsplat), where the method improves convergence speed while including initialization overhead in the reported time.

Insightful diagnostic ablations, including Gaussian trajectory length in parameter space (Fig. 5), comparisons across different matcher backbones (RoMa, LoFTR, DKM, RAFT, and monocular depth), and noise/hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.
weaknesses: Mathematical presentation errors in Section 3.3: The projection formulation is unconventional and contains inconsistencies. Specifically, camera projection matrices are described as 4x3 matrices mapping R^4 to R^3 via row multiplication, but in Eq. (6), vector b is defined as a vector of zeros b = [0, 0, 0, 0]^T. If b = 0, solving the least squares problem argmin ||A g_k + b||^2 would trivially yield g_k = 0; the constant affine component from the 4th homogeneous coordinate component must be non-zero.

Pre-processing dependency and pipeline complexity: While the dense matcher initialization removes the densification loop, it relies on a heavy pretrained model (RoMa) and multi-view overlap selection. The approach still requires camera poses (typically obtained from COLMAP), meaning the overall pipeline is not fully independent of traditional SfM.

Performance on specularities and unbounded backgrounds: As noted by the authors, initialization from 2D pixel colors struggles with view-dependent reflective surfaces, which explains why PSNR gains are less pronounced than LPIPS/SSIM gains. Additionally, distant unbounded regions (e.g., sky or peripheral background) can suffer from missing matches unless dense coverage is present.

strengths: Compelling conceptual shift: Replacing the iterative, heuristic densification process of 3DGS with a one-shot dense initialization via 2D dense correspondence triangulation is intuitive, elegant, and directly addresses a core bottleneck in Gaussian Splatting.

Strong empirical efficiency and rendering quality: The method achieves competitive or superior perceptual metrics (SSIM and LPIPS) across standard benchmarks (Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending) while using significantly fewer Gaussians (~40% fewer) and reaching target quality in a fraction of the optimization steps (e.g., at 5k iterations).

Orthogonality and modularity: The paper demonstrates that this dense initialization strategy can be cleanly integrated with other acceleration techniques (such as Taming 3DGS), yielding further speedups.

Thorough empirical analysis: The manuscript includes insightful analyses, notably quantifying the Gaussian trajectory/travel distance in parameter space (confirming that well-initialized splats move significantly less), robust ablation on noise tolerance, comparison across matching backbones (RoMa, LoFTR, DKM, DepthFM), and hyperparameter sensitivities.
weaknesses: Mathematical presentation issues in Section 3.3: In Section 3.3, camera projection matrices $P^i$ and $P^j$ are stated to be $4 \times 3$ rather than standard $3 \times 4$. Furthermore, in Equation (6), $b$ is defined as an all-zero vector $[0, 0, 0, 0]^T$; minimizing $\|A g_k^x + b\|^2$ with $b=0$ admits the trivial solution $g_k^x = 0$ unless affine inhomogeneous coordinates or rank constraints (SVD) are explicitly formulated. The linear triangulation derivation needs rigorous correction.

Lack of detail on Gaussian pruning: The paper claims to 'eliminate densification', but Figure A5 shows that the number of Gaussians decreases over optimization steps (from normalized ~0.9 to ~0.6). The main text should clearly clarify whether opacity-based pruning or periodic dead-splat removal is retained, and how this impacts overall parameter dynamics.

Scalability and dependency on dense matchers: While initialization time is included in the reported benchmarks, the dense matching phase (e.g., with RoMa) introduces external dependencies and heavy forward-pass overhead that scales with the number of selected neighbor pairs, which could be cumbersome for very large-scale or uncalibrated captures.
